request.system: You are a senior clinical coder in an Australian public hospital with fifteen years of experience coding inpatient episodes in ICD-10-AM. You are careful, conservative, and you never invent a code you are not sure of the chapter for.

messages.content:
Code the episode of care below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed. Give the three-character ICD-10-AM category for the principal diagnosis.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: [REDACTED]
Age: 58 years
Gender: Male
Date of Admission: June 8, 2020
Date of Discharge: [REDACTED]

Reason for Admission:
The patient was admitted on June 8, 2020, due to increased oxygen requirements following a COVID-19 diagnosis.

Hospital Course:
The patient received high flow nasal cannula therapy on admission. However, on hospital day 6, mechanical ventilation (MV) was initiated due to respiratory distress, hypoxemia, and hypercapnia. Despite MV, the patient's respiratory failure continued to worsen. Therefore, venovenous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO) was implemented on hospital day 11. Meropenem, levofloxacin, convalescent plasma therapy, and dexamethasone were administered during the treatment course.

Outcome:
The patient showed gradual improvement in lung compliance and chest radiography. Ultimately, VV-ECMO was discontinued on hospital day 38.

Follow-Up Care:
The patient will continue to receive follow-up care and monitoring as required for complete recovery.
Primary Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]Secondary Diagnoses: [diagnosis section withheld]
Co-Morbidities:
None

Procedures Performed:
MV and VV-ECMO were performed during hospitalization.

Medications Upon Discharge:
There were no medications prescribed at the time of discharge.

Recommendations:
The patient was advised to continue following a healthy lifestyle routine and receiving regular medical checkups.

Clinical Team:
- Attending Physician: [REDACTED]
- Nurse: [REDACTED]
- ECMO Specialist: [REDACTED]
- Respiratory Therapist: [REDACTED]
- Pharmacist: [REDACTED]
- Social Worker: [REDACTED]

Discharge Instructions:
The patient was advised to rest and follow a healthy routine as per routine health guidelines. The patient was informed of follow-up appointments and instructed to contact the hospital in case of any concerns or queries.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
**CODE: U07**

The principal diagnosis is COVID-19 (U07.1, COVID-19 virus identified). The discharge summary states the admission was "due to increased oxygen requirements following a COVID-19 diagnosis," so the viral infection is the condition chiefly responsible for the episode. The respiratory failure, hypoxaemia, and hypercapnia that followed are manifestations of that infection and would be coded as additional diagnoses, not as principal. The mechanical ventilation and VV-ECMO are procedures, not diagnoses.

The diagnosis section is withheld in this summary, so I have based this on the reason for admission and hospital course. Coding should be confirmed against the full medical record and the attending physician's documented diagnoses.
